findings.source_quote: Ellie’s father was resting in a hammock out on the lawn while the rest of the family tried to find the most comfortable place to seek relief from the heat.
findings.suggested_fix: Translate the common noun "hammock" into standard Indonesian rather than leaving the English word. For example: "Ayah Ellie sedang beristirahat di sebuah hamok (ayunan) di halaman rumput" or simply "Ayah Ellie sedang beristirahat di sebuah ayunan/hamok di halaman rumput." Preserve original sentence HTML structure and punctuation.
findings.translation_quote: Ayah Ellie sedang beristirahat di hammock di halaman rumput sementara anggota keluarga lainnya mencoba mencari tempat paling nyaman untuk mengurangi panas.

findings.source_quote: Indeed, the roof had been cleanly stripped away and the gable ends stoically stood there, holding up nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the parenthetical English and translate the architectural term into natural Indonesian. For example: "Memang, atap itu tersingkap bersih dan ujung-ujung gonjong berdiri tegak tanpa menyangga apa pun." Or: "...dan ujung-ujung atap (gonjong) berdiri tegak..." Keep the same sentence structure and HTML.
findings.translation_quote: Memang, atap itu tersingkap bersih dan ujung-ujung gonjong (gable) berdiri tegak tanpa menyangga apa pun.

findings.source_quote: The family gathered on the sunporch to watch the approaching storm.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more natural, standard Indonesian term for "sunporch". Suggested translations: "serambi bercahaya", "serambi", or simply "teras". Example: "Keluarga berkumpul di serambi untuk menyaksikan badai yang mendekat." Preserve HTML and punctuation.
findings.translation_quote: Keluarga berkumpul di teras yang menghadap matahari untuk menyaksikan badai yang mendekat.
